reason: The Egyptian elite are portrayed distinctly unfavorably throughout this passage. Pharaoh is depicted as stubbornly resistant to God's will, with his heart repeatedly 'hardened' (יְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה), causing him to refuse repeatedly to release the Israelites despite the mounting plagues. The Egyptian magicians/wise men (חַרְטֻמִּ֗ים) are shown as completely powerless and impotent—unable even to stand before Moses due to the plague of boils (וְלֹֽא־ יָכְל֣וּ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֗ים לַעֲמֹ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה). Both groups are portrayed as defeated by divine power, afflicted by the plagues alongside their subjects, and fundamentally unable to resist or protect themselves or their people.
